findings.body: The harness requires mock OTP but does not constrain `BIND_HOST`. The unchanged startup path at `backend/src/main.ts:56` gives an inherited `BIND_HOST` precedence over the mock provider's loopback default, so `BIND_HOST=0.0.0.0` exposes this server while any seeded administrator can authenticate with the fixed mock code. Because the browser flow may contain real-source financial data, the Playwright configuration must override or reject every bind address except `127.0.0.1`.
findings.title: Do not let the mock-OTP proof server bind beyond loopback

findings.body: The environment checks pin the Postgres write connection but omit `WAREHOUSE_DRIVER`. In unchanged `backend/src/core/core.module.ts:31-33`, inherited values `mysql` or `http` select a StarRocks adapter, while the ingestion endpoints still write the generated workbook to local Postgres. A developer environment configured for StarRocks can therefore make report/export/drill requests read a non-disposable, potentially live warehouse during this supposedly isolated proof. Require `WAREHOUSE_DRIVER=postgres` before starting either server.
findings.title: Pin report reads to the disposable Postgres warehouse

findings.body: `resolve()` only normalizes the path text; it does not resolve a pre-existing symlink or junction. The predictable default `3f-financial-legacy-ui-evidence` can therefore be linked from the temporary directory to the checkout or another untrusted location, pass all following `relative()`/basename checks, and receive real-source screenshots and evidence JSON. Canonicalize the created directory with `realpath` and verify the canonical target remains under the temporary task root and outside the checkout before any write.
findings.title: Resolve the evidence directory before writing financial screenshots

findings.body: The browser export proof checks only the suggested filename and that Playwright can create a stream. Any completed download—including an empty, corrupt, or wrong workbook—returns a non-null stream, so a regression in the HTTP/export/UI path would still pass. The required user-facing export baseline needs to consume the download, load it as a workbook, and compare its relevant sheets and financial values with the independently recorded baseline; the backend service-level snapshot does not exercise this browser path.
findings.title: Not done: downloaded legacy workbook contents match the baseline
